messages.subject: Re: Can't Analyze protein(s) for comparison
messages.body_plain:
Hello All,

I have tracked down this issue.

My workflow generates R scripts to run MSstats in an automated manner.  We were executing MSstats, and R, through the Rscript interface, which gave the following type of behavior:

...
Testing a comparison for protein  sp|Q9WV35|ABEC2_MOUSE ( 623  of  634 )
*** error : can't analyze sp|Q9WV35|ABEC2_MOUSE for comparison.
Testing a comparison for protein  sp|Q9WV55|VAPA_MOUSE ( 624  of  634 )
*** error : can't analyze sp|Q9WV55|VAPA_MOUSE for comparison.
Testing a comparison for protein  sp|Q9Z0X1|AIFM1_MOUSE ( 625  of  634 )
*** error : can't analyze sp|Q9Z0X1|AIFM1_MOUSE for comparison.
Testing a comparison for protein  sp|Q9Z1E4|GYS1_MOUSE ( 626  of  634 )
*** error : can't analyze sp|Q9Z1E4|GYS1_MOUSE for comparison.
Testing a comparison for protein  sp|Q9Z1P6|NDUA7_MOUSE ( 627  of  634 )
*** error : can't analyze sp|Q9Z1P6|NDUA7_MOUSE for comparison.
Testing a comparison for protein  sp|Q9Z1Q2|ABHGA_MOUSE ( 628  of  634 )
Testing a comparison for protein  sp|Q9Z1T2|TSP4_MOUSE ( 629  of  634 )
*** error : can't analyze sp|Q9Z1T2|TSP4_MOUSE for comparison.
Testing a comparison for protein  sp|Q9Z204|HNRPC_MOUSE ( 630  of  634 )
*** error : results of Protein sp|Q9Z204|HNRPC_MOUSE for comparison MDX are NA because there are measurements only in Group MDX.
Testing a comparison for protein  sp|Q9Z2I0|LETM1_MOUSE ( 631  of  634 )
*** error : can't analyze sp|Q9Z2I0|LETM1_MOUSE for comparison.
Testing a comparison for protein  sp|Q9Z2I9|SUCB1_MOUSE ( 632  of  634 )
*** error : can't analyze sp|Q9Z2I9|SUCB1_MOUSE for comparison.
Testing a comparison for protein  sp|Q9Z2Y3|HOME1_MOUSE ( 633  of  634 )
*** error : can't analyze sp|Q9Z2Y3|HOME1_MOUSE for comparison.
Testing a comparison for protein  sp|Q9Z2Z6|MCAT_MOUSE ( 634  of  634 )
*** error : can't analyze sp|Q9Z2Z6|MCAT_MOUSE for comparison.

After ditching Rscript to run our script, and moving to executing the exact same commands via the following syntax:
R < MSstats_Script.Rscript --vanilla

Our behavior has become as we would have hoped, as below:

Testing a comparison for protein  sp|Q9WV35|ABEC2_MOUSE ( 623  of  634 )
Testing a comparison for protein  sp|Q9WV55|VAPA_MOUSE ( 624  of  634 )
Testing a comparison for protein  sp|Q9Z0X1|AIFM1_MOUSE ( 625  of  634 )
Testing a comparison for protein  sp|Q9Z1E4|GYS1_MOUSE ( 626  of  634 )
Testing a comparison for protein  sp|Q9Z1P6|NDUA7_MOUSE ( 627  of  634 )
Testing a comparison for protein  sp|Q9Z1Q2|ABHGA_MOUSE ( 628  of  634 )
Testing a comparison for protein  sp|Q9Z1T2|TSP4_MOUSE ( 629  of  634 )
Testing a comparison for protein  sp|Q9Z204|HNRPC_MOUSE ( 630  of  634 )
*** error : results of Protein sp|Q9Z204|HNRPC_MOUSE for comparison MDX are NA because there are measurements only in Group MDX.
Testing a comparison for protein  sp|Q9Z2I0|LETM1_MOUSE ( 631  of  634 )
Testing a comparison for protein  sp|Q9Z2I9|SUCB1_MOUSE ( 632  of  634 )
Testing a comparison for protein  sp|Q9Z2Y3|HOME1_MOUSE ( 633  of  634 )
Testing a comparison for protein  sp|Q9Z2Z6|MCAT_MOUSE ( 634  of  634 )

Interestingly, this behavior was true under MRO 3.3 and CRAN R 3.4, on Windows (Win10Pro//Win Server 2008) and Linux (Fedora Core 20) systems.
While we don't know what the root cause is, we will avoid running MSstats through the Rscript interface.

I hope this information may be useful to someone else who finds themselves in this same situation.

Best wishes,
William

messages.subject: Processing problem with fractionation experiment in Progenesis
messages.subject_clean: Processing problem with fractionation experiment in Progenesis
messages.body_plain:
Hi Meena,

We performed an experiment in which we fractionated samples via HILIC, analyzed by LCMS, aligned in Progenesis QI-P, and then combined the 10 fractions into a single experiment in Progenesis. I have exported the abundances as normal and would now like to process in MSstats. However, I keep getting error messages and am not sure how to address them. Since Progenesis does a normalization for each fraction when they're recombined, the exported abundances are normalized - we do not get raw abundances. There's also a column titled "Fraction" that tells which fraction a particular feature came from; I deleted that column in order to make the format more consistent with what comes from a regular experiment. I also cheated a bit and renamed Normalized abundances to Raw abundances, and now I'm getting the following error message:
Error in which(colnames(input) == "Raw.abundance"):(which(colnames(input) ==  :
  argument of length 0
My recurring error messages are variations on this same theme. I've looked in the manual and online and cannot figure out what I might be doing wrong. In case it makes any difference, I'm running the newest version of MSstats (3.7.3) within RStudio.

Thanks in advance for your help!
Cheryl

messages.subject: Re: paired significance analysis on fractionated data
messages.subject_clean: paired significance analysis on fractionated data
messages.body_plain:
Dear Silvia,

In the current version, MSstats doesn't require the fractionation information. MSstats tries to recognize the fractionation information from overlapped feature, when there is no technical replicate. (When there is no technical replicate, the combination of condition and biological replicate is unique information for sample). But, it could be the issue if there are technical replicates. We plan to update MSstats more for the fractionation experiment during the summer.

Hope to help.

Sincerely,
- Meena
